items: Calculate Your Total Damages: Add up every payment you made to the contractor including the deposit, progress payments, and any materials you purchased separately to establish your exact financial loss.

Document Out-of-Pocket Costs: Track and calculate all expenses you incurred because the contractor failed to perform such as emergency equipment rentals, emergency repair bills, and storage fees for materials.
Calculate Replacement Contractor Costs: Compare your original contract price against what you paid a new contractor to finish the work and document that dollar difference as a recoverable damage.

Complete the Loss Worksheet: Fill out a written damage summary that lists each expense category with its dollar amount and supporting documentation source so you know precisely what to claim in court.

Screenshot Text Conversations: Take screenshots of every text and WhatsApp conversation with the contractor showing full timestamps visible so their broken promises and excuses are permanently preserved.
Export Conversations to Email: Use your phone's export function to send text conversation copies to a dedicated email account you control, creating a timestamped backup of all communications.

Save Evidence in Two Locations: Email screenshots and exported conversations to yourself and also upload them to cloud storage so you have redundant copies that won't disappear if one account is lost.
Preserve Voicemails Immediately: Forward any relevant voicemails to your dedicated case email folder before they auto-delete, or transcribe them verbatim and save the audio file to cloud storage.
Send a Written Demand Letter: Write and send a formal demand letter stating the exact amount owed, referencing your contract and evidence, with a specific deadline of 15 to 30 days for payment.

Organize Documents by Category: Sort all your evidence into folders labeled by claim category including deposits, additional payments, emergency costs, and replacement contractor expenses for easy courtroom access.
Verify Court Filing Requirements: Contact your local small claims court to confirm the exact filing fee based on your claim amount and obtain the required forms before attempting to file.

File Your Claim Accurately: Submit your completed claim form with your exact total damage amount, the contractor's full legal name and address, and copies of your supporting documentation to the court clerk.
